Discovering governing equations directly from observational data is a key step towards 
interpretable scientific machine learning. Current data-driven approaches typically operate on a 
single dataset, inherently limiting their performance when faced with restricted observations. In 
practice, multiple datasets are often available for the same physical system, distinguished only 
by distinct initial conditions or boundary configurations.  Here, we present a competitive 
optimization framework designed to discover shared partial differential equations (PDEs) from 
multi-source datasets , termed MCO -PDE. The framework first trains independent neural 
surrogates for each data source, and then employs a soft-competitive weighting mechanism to 
dynamically assess dataset credibility and aggregate a consensus global coefficient. Integrated 
with a genetic algorithm for structural search,

evidence.excerpt:
mechanism. Rather than treating every dataset equally, 
MCO-PDE assigns each dataset a credibility score based on three diagnostics, including the 
regression residual of the PDE, the condition number of the design matrix, and a leave -out 
generalization error. These scores are converted into softmax weights that determine each 
dataset's contribution to a global coefficient estimate; the global coefficients in turn drive a 
unified PDE loss that regularizes all surrogates simultaneously. An exponential moving 
average (EMA) of the global coefficients prevents oscillation and ensures stable convergence. 
The equation-structure search is performed by a genetic algorithm that generates and evolves 
candidate genome representations of PDEs based on the competitive optimization outcomes. 
The MCO-PDE framework is validated on a broad suite of canonical PDEs ranging from one

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Recovered equations are benchmarked directly against prescribed true PDEs across synthetic cases and against physically expected stage-dependent wave dynamics in experimental data.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by comparing discovered symbolic structures and coefficients against known analytical ground-truth PDEs, baseline method outputs, and physically interpretable wave-tank regimes.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system is optimized through surrogate data-fidelity loss, PDE residual loss, and genetic-search loss, with case weights and global coefficients derived from support-set least-squares fits, query residuals, and design-matrix condition numbers.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims regarding sample efficiency, robustness to noisy or irregular observations, and the ability to extract physically consistent governing equations align directly with the empirical results and parametric error bars provided.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is comprehensively evaluated across synthetic canonical PDEs (Burgers, KdV, Allen-Cahn, Klein-Gordon), high-dimensional and irregular boundary domains, heterogeneous porous media flow, and real laboratory wave-tank data, demonstrating clear comparative advantages over seven baseline methods adapted by majority voting under sparse data.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Discovered functional forms and recovered coefficients are benchmarked directly against known true analytical PDEs and compared systematically against seven existing baseline methods.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Direct comparison of discovered PDE symbolic structures and parameters against analytical ground-truth PDEs, baseline method outputs, and physical regime consistency in wave-tank data.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Neural surrogate MSE data loss, PDE residual loss, and genetic search loss computed from support-set least squares fits and credibility weighting.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly delineate assumptions, including the requirement that datasets share an identical governing structure and coefficients, as well as the substantial computational expense of repeatedly optimizing neural surrogates during the genetic search.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing neural surrogate fitting via automatic differentiation, least-squares coefficient fitting on support subsets, credibility weighting based on query residual and design matrix condition number, EMA global coefficient updates, and model selection via a physics-informed information criterion.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents an impactful, well-formulated, and rigorously tested approach to multi-source PDE discovery that directly resolves significant failure modes of existing single-source discovery techniques under sparse observations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript proposes MCO-PDE, a multi-source PDE discovery framework that couples independent neural network surrogates across diverse datasets with a soft-competitive weighting mechanism and genetic-algorithm structure search to discover shared governing equations under sparse or noisy conditions.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper presents an impactful, well-formulated, and rigorously tested approach to multi-source PDE discovery that directly resolves significant failure modes of existing single-source discovery techniques under sparse observations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly delineate assumptions, including the requirement that datasets share an identical governing structure and coefficients, as well as the substantial computational expense of repeatedly optimizing neural surrogates during the genetic search.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
